findings.title: Journal page error state has no retry and shows raw validation text; long search makes the page fail
findings.steps: Open /journal and type or paste a search longer than 80 characters (the input has no maxlength), or open /journal?q=<81 chars>.
findings.expected: The input limits or explains the length. Any load error offers a Retry button.
findings.actual: The API returns 422 and the page swaps the list for an alert reading 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'. There is no retry button. When a load fails for any other reason (server down, timeout), the only way back is to edit the search or reload.
findings.evidence: SSR of /journal?q=aaaa…(81) rendered <div class="alert alert--error">Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters. journal.vue has no retry control in its error branch.

findings.title: Plant detail journal load error has no retry
findings.steps: Open a plant while GET /api/journal fails (server error or timeout).
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that refetches the journal.
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage 'Could not load the journal.' is shown. No retry is offered, so the user has to reload or add an entry.
findings.evidence: pages/plants/[id].vue: <AlertMessage v-if="journalLoadError"> has no retry action, although refreshJournal exists.

findings.title: No 10-second timeout on journal requests
findings.where: All journal fetches and mutations (useApiClient / useApiFetch)
findings.steps: Make the API hang (slow network) and then add, edit, delete or search entries.
findings.expected: Requests fail after 10 s with a visible error, and the buttons become usable again.
findings.actual: $fetch.create sets no timeout. 'Saving…' stays disabled and 'Loading entries…' stays on screen for as long as the request hangs.
findings.evidence: composables/useApi.ts: $fetch.create({ baseURL, credentials, headers, onResponseError }) has no timeout. The journal code adds none.

findings.title: Retrying an add after a timeout or lost response creates duplicate entries
findings.steps: Submit an entry. The server saves it but the response is lost or slow. The user clicks Add entry again.
findings.actual: Every POST inserts a new row. There is no idempotency key or duplicate check, so the retry adds a second identical entry.
findings.evidence: journal.py create_entry runs a plain INSERT. The client sends no request id.

findings.title: Entries with emoji or other non-BMP text: limit mismatch, and edit refuses to save
findings.steps: 1) In the form, type emoji: typing stops at 250 emoji while the counter says 0 characters left, even though the server accepts 500. 2) Create an entry of 500 emoji (accepted by the API, 201), then click Edit and Save without changing anything.
findings.expected: Client and server count characters the same way, and an existing valid entry can be edited.
findings.actual: The client counts UTF-16 code units (maxlength and .length), while the server counts code points. Editing the 500-emoji entry shows '-500 characters left' and is refused with 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.'
findings.evidence: POST with body = '🌱'*500 returned 201. JournalEntryForm validate() uses form.body.trim().length > 500, and the textarea uses maxlength=500.

findings.title: Out-of-range ids crash journal endpoints with 500
findings.steps: curl POST /api/journal with plant_id 999999999999999999999, or GET /api/journal?plant_id=99999999999999999999, or PUT/DELETE /api/journal/99999999999999999999.
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (the SQLite integer overflows).
findings.evidence: All four requests returned 'Internal Server Error [500]'. The id fields have no upper bound.

findings.title: Control characters such as NUL are accepted in journal text
findings.expected: Refused with a 4xx and a reason, or sanitised.
findings.actual: Stored as-is (201) and later rendered in the feed.

findings.title: Today's date can be refused when browser and server time zones differ
findings.steps: Use the app from a time zone ahead of the server (e.g. UTC+13 in the morning) and add an entry with the default date (browser 'today').
findings.actual: The server compares against its own date.today() and answers 'Journal date cannot be in the future.'
findings.evidence: Client uses todayIso() (browser local time). Server uses date.today() (server local time). The request 2026-11-13 was refused while the server date was 2026-11-12.

findings.title: Long plant names overflow the Journal feed at 375 px
findings.steps: Create a plant named with 80 characters and no spaces, add a journal entry, then view /journal at 375 px wide.
findings.expected: The name wraps inside the card.
findings.actual: .journal-feed__plant has no overflow-wrap (only .journal-entry__body has it), so the link pushes the card wider and the page scrolls sideways.
findings.evidence: main.css: overflow-wrap: anywhere is applied only to .journal-entry__body. Plant names allow up to 80 characters.

findings.title: 'edited' label missing for edits made within the same second
findings.steps: Add an entry and edit it immediately.
findings.actual: edited compares updated_at !== created_at, and both have one-second resolution, so a quick edit shows no label.
findings.evidence: Both timestamps use datetime('now'), which has second precision.
